top_story: Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz set the basis for a wider confrontation, and Iranian officials signaled then that any such move would push retaliation across the Gulf. By 28–29 June, that warning had materialized into direct US-Iran crossfire that spilled into Bahrain and Kuwait, eroding a fragile interim peace track and sharpening the struggle over Hormuz. This escalation unfolded as Israel struck displaced Palestinians sheltering in beach tents in Gaza on 25 June, underscoring how regional coercion is falling most heavily on civilians even when the immediate flashpoints differ. The regional picture is now defined by linked military escalation and collapsing political restraint, with Gulf insecurity and civilian vulnerability rising together.
